jobs.description:
Job Description

This position has been deemed critical by the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring pause.

This position is based on Stanford’s main campus with consideration given to the option for a hybrid work schedule (partially onsite 3 or more days a week), subject to operational need.

Interested candidates must include a resume and cover letter to be considered for this position.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa.

About Us

The Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability strives to create a future when humans and nature thrive in concert and in perpetuity. The school is made up of a three-part structure to drive global impact: Our academic departments and programs educate students and create new knowledge across areas of research that are crucial for advancing the long-term prosperity of the planet and people; Institutes bridge scholarship at Stanford and beyond, bringing multiple viewpoints to bear on urgent challenges; The Sustainability Accelerator drives new policy and technology solutions through a worldwide network of partners who work with our teams to develop solutions at a global scale. The school is dedicated to creating and supporting a community with the richness of experience and background needed to create solutions that benefit all people, particularly those most affected by environmental damage and climate change.

For more information on the school, click here .

Precourt Institute for Energy

As part of the Stanford Doerr School of Sustainability , the Precourt Institute for Energy concentrates the talents of the University on energy research and education, from basic science and technology to policy and business. Our mission is to spark the creativity, collaboration, learning, and leadership needed for the global energy transformation. The initiatives, research centers, and educational programs of the Precourt Institute connect across campus in all seven of Stanford’s schools supporting work with the potential to solve the toughest energy challenges from science and engineering to policy and economics. We also build collaborations globally with industry, other research institutions, government, and civic organizations in pursuit of sustainable, affordable, secure energy for all people.

Position Overview

The Precourt Institute for Energy seeks exceptional candidates for the role of Executive Director, Partnerships & Strategy
. Reporting directly to and working closely with the Precourt Institute Director, the Executive Director will spearhead the development and execution of a comprehensive strategy that integrates the academic and practitioner perspectives, capabilities and resources across the research, development and deployment pipeline to advance sustainable, affordable and secure energy for all.

Working with the Institute director, faculty fellows, staff and advisory council, the Executive Director will design and build a cohesive fabric to enable the Institute’s centers, initiative and programs (as well as other units across Stanford) to sustain thriving, multi-faceted partnerships with industry and non-profit organizations. The expected outcome is that Stanford partners with practitioners and delivers research impact across all facets of the energy system such that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.

The role will spearhead the development and growth of large, funded partnerships and alliances with industry and non-profit organizations, by leveraging the breadth and depth of expertise among Stanford faculty and researchers and by coordinating with centers, initiatives and programs in the Institute and with other units across Stanford. The Executive Director will represent the institute in senior-level strategic discussions and engage with energy leaders.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Develop and execute a strategic vision and plan that integrates academic and practitioner perspectives, capabilities and resources to advance Stanford’s mission across the entire energy system.
Create and strengthen connective tissues to bring together specific domains of energy research through strategic convenings and grantmaking.
Deliver significant funded partnerships between Stanford, industry and non-profit organizations.
Coordinate with centers, initiatives program and stakeholders across Stanford to catalyze research and partnerships that spans all facets of energy.
Lead and manage a team supporting complex energy research programs and partnerships, including technical experts and professionals responsible for partnership development, faculty engagement, grantmaking, and program execution.
Ensure successful execution of funded programs by monitoring progress, managing risks, and maintaining accountability for sponsor expectations and contractual commitments.
Serve as a senior liaison to management, cross-functional areas, schools, sponsors, and other external organizations.

In addition to the minimum qualifications listed below, our preferred qualifications include:

PhD degree and 15 years of relevant experience or combination of education and relevant experience. Advanced degree may be required.
Exceptional understanding of the energy technology ecosystem.
Exceptional communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders, including senior government officials and corporate executives.
Strategic thinker with the ability to connect technological innovation with economic and policy considerations.
Demonstrated ability to identify, develop, and cultivate strategic partnerships across academia, industry, and government.
Proven ability to resolve complex issues quickly and make sound decisions that advance university objectives within a collaborative culture.

The expected pay range for this position is $214,936 to $260,287 per annum.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Provide strategy and vision; make decisions that establish objectives for the overall direction or operation of a significant project(s) or area(s).
Manage staff of a large science, engineering, and/or technical research area, which includes recruiting, hiring, developing, evaluating and setting priorities; manage business, technical, and educational activities for direct reports including managers and technical experts.
Identify, clarify, and resolve issues with strategic impact and substantial significance, which span multiple areas, using advanced technical and professional knowledge requiring broad discretion and judgment.
Collaborate with others on the direction of activities relevant to long-term objectives. Develop strategies to ensure effective achievement of objectives.
Develop policies and procedures as they relate to academic or program activities.
Implement, evaluate and maintain quality control standards to ensure program success.
Establish, oversee and manage financials and schedule for large programs and/or multiple projects.
Recommend the adoption of emerging technologies and the development of new methods and approaches.
Negotiate with internal departments and external agencies with authority to commit resources and effort.
Serve as a liaison to senior management, cross-functional areas, schools and external organizations such as sponsors and government agencies.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree and eight years of relevant experience or combination of education and relevant experience. Advanced degree may be required.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Experience leading, managing, motivating and developing technical staff.
Experience leading complex scientific, engineering or technical research projects or programs.
Detailed understanding of relevant business and technical knowledge and problem resolution.
Ability to synthesize and articulate technical and scientific methodologies, specifications, and information.

Demonstrated ability to work and communicate effectively with others. .

Ability to influence and establish effective working relationships in a diverse environment.
Ability to resolve complex issues quickly and make decisions that meet university objectives in a collaborative culture.

Description

The Scientific Program Director provides high-level scientific, regulatory, and operational leadership in support of science research programs within the assigned department. Working closely with Principal Investigator, faculty, research staff, trainees, institutional offices, administration, and external collaborators, this individual manages complex research initiatives from proposal development through execution and reporting.

The position serves as the primary administrative partner to faculty and trainees for sponsored research activities, including grant development, regulatory compliance, scientific reporting, project coordination, and research operations. The Senior Research Program Manager oversees multiple concurrent research programs, facilitates multidisciplinary collaborations, monitors project milestones and deliverables, coordinates regulatory submissions, and develops systems that support efficient and compliant research administration.

This role requires a strong scientific background in genetics, neuroscience, molecular biology, or related discipline, exceptional organizational and communication skills, and the ability to translate complex research objectives into effective operational plans.

Responsibilities

Serve as the primary administrative and scientific contact for multiple research programs and complex multi-investigator initiatives, supporting studies utilizing both in vitro cellular systems and in vivo mouse models.
Collaborating with PIs to coordinate project timelines, milestones, deliverables, and reporting requirements for federal and nonfederal funded research programs.
Coordinate scientific meetings, advisory committee meetings, program reviews, and collaborative working groups by preparing agendas, assembling meeting materials, documenting action items, and tracking follow-up activities.
Work closely with Mount Sinai Innovation Partners (MSIP) to coordinate collaborations among investigators, institutional departments, and external research partners.
Assist investigators with scientific preparation and submission of federal and non-federal grant applications.
Coordinate preparation of RPPRs, Just-in-Time submissions, supplements, and sponsor-required documentation.
Preparation of data request submissions and annual progress reports to BioMe and public repositories (e.g. dbGaP, NIAGADs, NCRAD, UK Biobank).
Partner with departmental pre-award and post-award grants administration teams to assist with budget development, monitor expenditures, review financial reports, identify spending trends, and ensure compliance with sponsor guidelines and institutional policies.
Prepare, coordinate, and maintain regulatory documentation including IRB, IACUC, eSafety, biosafety, and other institutional compliance submissions, ensuring research activities remain compliant with federal, state, and institutional regulations.
Track protocol approvals, continuing reviews, amendments, and compliance deadlines.
Coordinate research operations including equipment acquisitions, facilities coordination, service contracts, and laboratory logistics.
Develop SOPs and administrative workflows that improve operational efficiency and regulatory compliance.
Support recruitment, onboarding, and mentoring of research personnel and junior administrative staff including screening candidates, interviewing technical staff, and working with HR on hiring and Labor Relations on termination.
Participates in departmental initiatives, operational planning, and other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education Requirements

PhD in Genetics, Neuroscience, Molecular Biology, Biomedical Sciences, or a closely related field required. Master's degree with significant experience in scientific research administration may be considered.

Experience Requirements

5–8 years supporting academic biomedical research programs.
Experience with NIH-funded grants and sponsored research administration.
Experience preparing grant applications, progress reports, and regulatory submissions.
Experience coordinating complex multi-investigator research programs.
Background in genetics, genomics, neuroscience, or molecular biology strongly preferred.

General Skills And Competencies

Strong scientific background with the ability to interpret biomedical research.
Knowledge of NIH funding mechanisms and grant administration.
Experience preparing IRB, IACUC, eSafety, and regulatory documentation.
Excellent scientific writing and editing skills.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously.
Excellent interpersonal and collaboration skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to work independently with sound judgment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and research administration software.
Experience using Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) or similar procurement and financial management systems is preferred.

The Mount Sinai Health System is committed to fostering an environment where everyone can contribute to excellence. We share a common dedication to delivering outstanding patient care. When you join us, you become part of Mount Sinai’s unparalleled legacy of achievement, education, and innovation as we work together to transform healthcare. Our leaders are expected to challenge outdated practices, promote a culture of respect, and work toward meaningful improvements that enhance patient care and workplace experiences. We are dedicated to building a supportive and welcoming environment where everyone has the opportunity to thrive and advance professionally. Explore this opportunity and be part of the next chapter in our history.

Mount Sinai Health System is one of the largest academic medical systems in the New York metro area, with more than 48,000 employees working across eight hospitals, more than 400 outpatient practices, more than 300 labs, a school of nursing, and a leading school of medicine and graduate education. Mount Sinai advances health for all people, everywhere, by taking on the most complex health care challenges of our time — discovering and applying new scientific learning and knowledge; developing safer, more effective treatments; educating the next generation of medical leaders and innovators; and supporting local communities by delivering high-quality care to all who need it. U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Children’s Hospitals” ranks Mount Sinai Kravis Children's Hospital among the country’s best in several pediatric specialties. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is ranked No. 11 nationwide in National Institutes of Health funding and in the 99th percentile in research dollars per investigator according to the Association of American Medical Colleges. Newsweek’s “The World’s Best Smart Hospitals” ranks The Mount Sinai Hospital as No. 1 in New York and in the top five globally, and Mount Sinai Morningside in the top 20 globally.

The Opportunity

The Washington State Department of Health (DOH) is seeking an experienced leader to serve as the Deputy Director of the Office of Enterprise Risk Management (OERM), within the Center for Facilities, Risk and Adjudication (CFRA).

The Office of Enterprise Risk Management
brings together more than 50 FTEs across Public Disclosure, Information Governance and Records Management, Privacy, External Audit and Internal Controls, Enterprise Risk Management, Workplace Safety, and Civil Rights and ADA. Together, these teams help DOH navigate complex challenges and manage risk, safeguard information, promote transparency and accountability, support equitable access, and meet legal and regulatory requirements.

The Deputy Director provides leadership across these varied functions, working closely with the OERM Director and program leaders to coordinate operations, anticipate and address complex challenges, strengthen systems and processes, and translate agency and office priorities into meaningful action. This position serves as a key thought partner to the Director and a core member of the OERM leadership team, with delegated authority to act on behalf of the Director when needed.

This is an opportunity for a strategic and collaborative leader to bring together people, programs, and perspectives to strengthen how this office supports the Department of Health and advances its mission to protect and improve the health of people in Washington.

Leading Office Operations

Partner with the OERM Director to provide strategic and operational direction, establish priorities, and advance shared goals across OERM.
Provide day-to-day leadership and coordination across OERM’s diverse programs and functions.
Translate agency and office priorities into actionable strategies, work plans, and measurable outcomes.
Serve as the Director’s delegate when needed and provide continuity of leadership across the office.
Serve as CFRA’s lead subject matter expert for legislative and rulemaking activities, coordinating CFRA’s response to proposed legislation, and helping program leaders understand and prepare for potential impacts.

Advancing Agency Partnerships & Shared Solutions

Identify opportunities for OERM to work across organizational boundaries and develop coordinated approaches to agency needs.
Help translate OERM’s expertise into practical guidance and solutions for staff across the agency.

Navigating Agency Risk & Compliance

Provide guidance to program staff and agency leaders as they navigate emerging challenges, competing risks and priorities, and legal, policy, and operational considerations. Facilitate problem-solving and help identify strategic solutions.
Help ensure OERM programs are well-positioned to support agency compliance with applicable laws, policies, and regulatory requirements.
Strengthen organizational practices that promote accountability, transparency, privacy, civil rights and equitable access, workplace safety, and responsible stewardship of agency resources.
Anticipate emerging issues and develop strategies to address them proactively.

Improving Systems & Processes

Evaluate office-wide systems, processes, and practices to identify and advance opportunities for greater coordination, efficiency, and effectiveness.
Use data, staff and partner perspectives, and continuous improvement practices to inform decision-making and identify opportunities for improvement.
Help develop sustainable approaches to operational challenges and changing office and agency needs.
Lead the development, implementation, maintenance, and review of agency policies and procedures related to OERM programs and activities.

Leading People & Strengthening Teams

Support OERM program leaders in navigating priorities, solving problems, delivering results, and advancing effective performance management and continuous improvement .
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, inclusion, and shared responsibility, where people feel heard and supported, and their ideas, strengths, and perspectives are valued.
Support leaders and staff through organizational change, emerging challenges, and evolving priorities.
Help cultivate strong connections across OERM’s teams and with partners throughout the agency.
Promote employee engagement, professional development, and opportunities for growth.
Supervise assigned staff, while also providing leadership, guidance, and support to other leaders and staff across the office .

Why You’ll Love This Role

This role offers the opportunity to influence work that reaches across every part of the Washington State Department of Health. OERM’s programs play an essential role in protecting information, promoting transparency and accountability, supporting civil rights and equitable access, managing risk, and ensuring safe and effective workplaces.

The Deputy Director will work alongside experienced program leaders and agency partners while helping bring together a wide range of expertise toward common goals. For a leader who enjoys solving complex problems, improving systems, building strong partnerships, and developing people—and who finds meaning in helping an organization work better for the people it serves.

Advanced knowledge and experience
interpreting and applying laws, regulations, and best practices in public disclosure/public records, audit, civil rights compliance, privacy compliance, or risk management. (Must have been gained within the last ten (10) years.)

experience

Overseeing and managing programs in public disclosure/public records, audit, civil rights compliance, privacy compliance, risk management, or legal affairs

Developing and implementing organization-wide policies and procedures
Leading significant initiatives involving organizational change, process improvement, or systems transformation that require coordination across programs

Work is performed using standard office furniture, equipment, and software such as a laptop, docking station, monitors, cellular phone, Microsoft Office products, Adobe Professional Pro, SharePoint, and other similar products.
